title: Three-pile shuffle group
W: Using the six ways to stack three piles in a perfect shuffle, which rearrangements of the deck can you reach?
M: Determine the subgroup of $S_{3n}$ generated by the six 3-pile perfect shuffles (all pile orders), for every $n$.

title: Jacobi matrix of primes
W: Use the primes as the off-diagonal entries of a Jacobi matrix. Known criteria for absolutely continuous spectrum just fail because prime gaps fluctuate. Decide the spectral type.
M: Let $J$ be the Jacobi matrix on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with $a_n=p_n$ (the $n$-th prime) and $b_n=0$, which is self-adjoint since $\sum1/p_n=\infty$. Decide whether the spectrum of $J$ is purely absolutely continuous on $\mathbb R$.

title: Two-frequency localization
W: Use a potential that is the sum of two cosines with frequencies √2 and √3, and take strong coupling. Prove electrons localize for these specific frequencies, not just for almost every frequency pair.
M: Let $(H_\theta\psi)(n)=\psi(n+1)+\psi(n-1)+10\big(\cos2\pi(n\sqrt2+\theta_1)+\cos2\pi(n\sqrt3+\theta_2)\big)\psi(n)$. Prove that for Lebesgue-a.e. $\theta\in\mathbb T^2$, $H_\theta$ has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.

title: Ringel for forests
W: Split a complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices into identical copies of any given forest with m edges.
M: Prove $K_{2m+1}$ decomposes into $2m+1$ copies of any forest with $m$ edges.

title: Monotile assembly threshold
W: With one tile shape, deciding whether a region can be tiled is easy in some cases; with many shapes it is hard. Find the smallest number of shapes where it becomes hard.
M: Find the least $t$ such that some fixed set of $t$ polygons makes "does this finite region admit an exact tiling?" NP-complete, and prove all sets of fewer polygons give polynomial-time problems.

title: Two vortices on a cube
W: Two identical point vortices on the surface of a cube have no symmetry to make them integrable. Show their motion is chaotic.
M: Let $G$ be the Green function of the flat unit-cube surface $S$ and $R$ its Robin function. Show the Hamiltonian $H(z_1,z_2)=G(z_1,z_2)+\tfrac12(R(z_1)+R(z_2))$ on $S\times S\setminus\Delta$, with symplectic form $dA_1+dA_2$, has an energy level on which the flow has positive topological entropy.

title: Rupert superballs
W: The cube can pass through a hole drilled in a copy of itself; the round ball cannot. Show every superball between them, |x|^p+|y|^p+|z|^p ≤ 1 with p > 2, can.
M: Let $B_p=\{|x|^p+|y|^p+|z|^p\le1\}$. Prove that for every $p\in(2,\infty)$ there are orthogonal projections $\pi_1,\pi_2$ onto planes and a rigid motion $\rho$ of the plane with $\rho(\pi_1(B_p))\subset\operatorname{int}\pi_2(B_p)$.

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
W: Show the largest prime factor of Markov numbers tends to infinity.
M: Prove $P(m)\to\infty$ as $m$ runs through Markov numbers.

title: Minimal-mass blow-up with reflection
W: In the 2D Schrödinger equation where each point feels the density at its mirror point, blow-up needs at least the ground-state mass. Classify the solutions that blow up with exactly that mass.
M: For $i u_t+\Delta u+|u(-x,t)|^2u=0$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with $\|u_0\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$ ($Q$ the cubic ground state), prove that every $H^1$ solution blowing up in finite time equals, up to phase and scaling, the pseudo-conformal transform of $Q$ centred at the origin.

title: Random Wang tiles
W: Pick n random tile types with colored edges. How likely are they to tile the plane?
M: For $n$ Wang tiles with edge colours i.i.d. uniform in $[c]$, find the asymptotics of $\Pr(\text{tiles }\mathbb{Z}^2)$ as $n\to\infty$.
